ok.de: Well steht direkt hinter may, ohne be: may well reject.
ok.en: Well stands right after may, without be: may well reject.

items.text: The client may be well reject our first offer, so we should prepare alternatives.

ok.de: Nach bound steht to und die Grundform: bound to get.
ok.en: After bound comes to and the base form: bound to get.

items.text: My sister is bound getting lost without a map, so I will drive her there.

ok.de: Mit dem Subjekt vorn folgt likely to und die Grundform.
ok.en: With the subject first, likely to and the base form follow.

items.text: The project is likely that finish a week late because of the delay.

ok.de: Englisch sagt there is, nicht it exists.
ok.en: English says there is, not it exists.

items.text: It exists a slim chance that the board will reject the budget.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Unlikely to + Grundform nennt eine unwahrscheinliche Handlung.
ok.en: No mistake: Unlikely to + base form names an improbable action.

items.text: Our neighbors are unlikely to move before the summer.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: There is a high chance that … nennt eine Möglichkeit.
ok.en: No mistake: There is a high chance that … names a possibility.

items.text: There is a high chance that the supplier will ask for an extension.

ok.de: Mit at the moment braucht es die Verlaufsform: are rising.
ok.en: With at the moment you need the continuous: are rising.

items.text: Prices in the sector rise at the moment, so we are reviewing our offers.

ok.de: Nach wondering folgt if und normale Satzstellung: if we could shift.
ok.en: After wondering comes if and normal word order: if we could shift.

items.text: I was wondering could we shift the review to Thursday afternoon.

ok.de: Erschöpfung ist ein Zustand, deshalb ohne being: is very exhausted.
ok.en: Exhaustion is a state, so no being: is very exhausted.

items.text: The client is being very exhausted after the long negotiation, so let us end early.

ok.de: Need ist ein Zustandsverb und bleibt einfach: We need.
ok.en: Need is a stative verb and stays simple: We need.

items.text: We are needing written confirmation before we can release the budget.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Silly beschreibt Verhalten, deshalb passt is being.
ok.en: No mistake: silly describes behavior, so is being fits.

items.text: My little brother is being silly today because he wants us to laugh.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Are hoping macht die Einladung freundlich und weich.
ok.en: No mistake: are hoping makes the invitation friendly and soft.

items.text: We are hoping to see you at the barbecue on Saturday.

ok.de: Der Plan liegt in der Vergangenheit: were going to.
ok.en: The plan lies in the past: were going to.

items.text: We are going to publish the report in March, but the board asked for changes.

ok.de: Nach about steht to und die Grundform: about to announce.
ok.en: After about comes to and the base form: about to announce.

items.text: The CEO was about announcing the merger when the news leaked.

ok.de: Aus der Vergangenheit auf Späteres: would later employ.
ok.en: From the past at something later: would later employ.

items.text: The startup began with three people in 2015 and will later employ two hundred.

ok.de: Für einen Plan in der Vergangenheit gilt was to: was to join.
ok.en: For a plan in the past was to is used: was to join.

items.text: The new director should join us in January, but she took another job.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Was about to + Grundform, dann kommt etwas dazwischen.
ok.en: No mistake: was about to + base form, then something intervenes.

items.text: I was about to leave the house when I noticed that the oven was still on.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Were going to nennt den Plan von damals.
ok.en: No mistake: were going to names the plan from back then.

items.text: We were going to move to Lisbon, but the flat prices changed our minds.

ok.de: Für „keiner von“ mit Nomen steht none of.
ok.en: For “not one of” with a noun none of is used.

items.text: No one of the shortlisted vendors has submitted a complete proposal.

ok.de: Hardly ist schon verneint, ein zweites not ist zu viel.
ok.en: Hardly is already negative, a second not is too much.

items.text: We did not hardly change the layout, only the colors.

ok.de: Die feste Form heißt no longer.
ok.en: The fixed form is no longer.

items.text: The platform is not longer available for customers in the EU.

ok.de: Bei the number of steht das Verb im Singular: has.
ok.en: With the number of the verb is singular: has.

items.text: The number of defects have fallen sharply since we changed supplier.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: Hardly any heißt „kaum“ und braucht kein not.
ok.en: No mistake: hardly any means “barely any” and needs no not.

items.text: There was hardly any traffic, so we arrived early.

ok.de: Kein Fehler: None of + Nomen heißt „keiner von“.
ok.en: No mistake: none of + noun means “not one of”.

items.text: None of my cousins lives in the same city as my parents.
